messages:
sam-infra: starting a serial apply for cross-region routing change (prod-east -> prod-west). change window 23:00-01:00 PT. pinning provider to 3.2.1 to avoid drift. deploybot will run canary then serial waves. flagging @infra-oncall.

maria: which tf workspaces/stacks are in scope?

sam-infra: stack list: network-core, vpc-attachments, transit-gw, iam-cross-account. plan already ran in canary-staging. main risk = TGW route churn + IAM trust policy add.

ben: please paste the plan summary for iam change (just the actions) — we need clear rollback path.

karen: plan excerpt:
```
# aws_iam_role.example
+ create
# aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.foo
- delete
+ create
# aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route.route
~ update in-place
```
Note: the new attachments are additive. older role remains.

sam-infra: rollback criteria (draft):
- if deploybot reports >2% increase in rejected connections from prod-west within 10m after any AZ wave -> rollback
- any traceroute showing traffic pinned to wrong region -> rollback
- terraform apply errors on >1 AZ -> pause and rollback
Rollback procedure:
1) trigger `deploybot rollback ${thread_ts}` (this will start revert apply using the previous tfstate snapshot)
2) verify route table counts and KMS access from prod-west before unpinning provider
3) set provider pin back only after revert succeeds and smoke tests pass
4) open incident channel and notify CS/SEs

deploybot: scheduled run queued. canary apply at 2026-03-22T23:00:00Z, serial waves every 10m. will post progress and failure signals. use `deploybot abort <ts>` to stop.

maria: ok, make sure canary targets a single AZ and has traffic-shadow rule 10% to prod-west. also set `max_parallelism = 1` for vpc-attachments during waves.

sam-infra: done. pushed quick config change to branch `routed-crossregion-pin` — will run canary plan again in 5m. notify if you see drift.

infra-oncall: i'll be oncall during window and will watch metrics (TCP reject, route flaps, host availability). can take revert if we see >normal flaps. ping me @infra-oncall.

ben: add explicit post-apply checks in runbook: one-liner S3 access + KMS decrypt + curl to internal health endpoint. if any fail, autoset rollback flag.

karen: re-run plan after pin change: no destructive deletes expected. leaving apply to deploybot. :thumbsup:

sam-infra: cool. if deploybot posts any `ERROR` or `FAILURE` messages, we follow rollback steps immediately. otherwise i'll squash leftover route diffs in a follow-up. thanks all.

deploybot: INFO: canary apply started — will log each wave.
